title: NJ Driver's Manual – Chapter 3
subtitle: Signs, Signals & Pavement Markings
note: Based on the 2025 NJ Driver's Manual, Chapter 3. Questions marked [image] show a road sign image in the quiz app. Verify all answers against the current manual before your exam.

questions.q: [image: stop sign] What does this sign mean?
opts: Slow down and proceed with caution
Come to a complete stop; yield to all traffic and pedestrians before proceeding
Yield to cross traffic only
Stop only if other vehicles are present
questions.exp: A stop sign requires a complete stop at the stop line (or crosswalk/intersection edge if no line). You must yield to all cross traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

questions.q: [image: yield sign] What does this sign mean?
opts: Come to a complete stop, then go
Slow down, check for traffic, and yield the right of way — stop only if necessary
Merge into the nearest lane immediately
Speed up to match the speed of cross traffic
questions.exp: A yield sign means slow down and be prepared to stop. You must give the right of way to vehicles and pedestrians in or approaching the intersection, but you need not stop unless necessary.

questions.q: [image: speed limit 55 sign] What does this sign indicate?
opts: The recommended speed for curves ahead
The minimum speed required on this roadway
The maximum lawful speed on this section of road under ideal conditions
The average speed of traffic measured at this location
questions.exp: A speed limit sign sets the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions. You may need to drive slower when conditions (weather, traffic, road surface) are less than ideal.

questions.q: [image: do not enter sign] What does this sign mean?
opts: Keep right — do not enter the left lane
You are about to exit a one-way road
You must not enter this road in the direction you are traveling
Road closed ahead for construction
questions.exp: A Do Not Enter sign means you are attempting to enter a one-way road in the wrong direction. Do not enter. This sign is often paired with a Wrong Way sign.

questions.q: [image: wrong way sign] A driver sees this sign. What does it mean?
opts: You have turned into the wrong lane and must move right
You are driving against the flow of traffic on a one-way road — turn around immediately
Road ends ahead; U-turn permitted
Wrong route chosen; take the next exit
questions.exp: A Wrong Way sign confirms that you are traveling against traffic on a one-way road. Pull over safely and turn around.

questions.q: [image: curve ahead warning sign] What does this sign warn you about?
opts: A sharp intersection ahead
A curve in the road ahead — slow down before entering
A detour route around construction
Lane ends ahead; merge left
questions.exp: A curve-ahead warning sign alerts you to an upcoming curve. Reduce speed before the curve and follow the safe advisory speed if posted.

questions.q: [image: railroad crossing sign] What does this sign indicate?
opts: A four-way stop intersection ahead
A traffic circle ahead
A railroad crossing ahead — be prepared to stop
A rest area and fuel station ahead
questions.exp: The round yellow RR crossing sign warns that railroad tracks cross the road ahead. Slow down, look and listen in both directions, and stop if a train is approaching.

questions.q: [image: school zone sign] What does this sign's shape and color tell you?
opts: It is a guide sign indicating a school building nearby
Its pentagonal (five-sided) yellow shape identifies a school zone — expect children and slow down
It is a regulatory sign requiring a complete stop during school hours
It is an orange construction sign near a school building
questions.exp: The pentagon (five-sided) shape is used exclusively for school zone and school crossing signs. Yellow color means warning. Slow to the posted school zone speed when children are present.

questions.q: [image: no U-turn sign] What does this sign prohibit?
opts: Left turns
Right turns
U-turns
Passing other vehicles
questions.exp: A No U-Turn sign (white rectangle with a red circle/slash over a U-turn arrow) means U-turns are prohibited at this location.

questions.q: [image: one way sign] What does this sign tell you about the road ahead?
opts: Traffic may travel in both directions in this lane
The road is a one-way street — travel only in the direction the arrow points
Merge ahead — all traffic must move in this direction
Priority road — you have the right of way
questions.exp: A One Way sign with an arrow means all traffic on that roadway must travel in the direction shown. Entering from the other end would mean driving the wrong way.

questions.q: [image: no passing zone pennant sign] What does this pennant-shaped sign indicate?
opts: A no-parking zone on this side of the road
The beginning of a no-passing zone — you may not pass other vehicles here
A yield zone where you must let faster traffic pass
An advisory speed zone for the curve ahead
questions.exp: The yellow pennant (triangle pointing right, on the left side of the road) marks the beginning of a no-passing zone. Passing is prohibited from this point until a Passing Permitted sign or broken centerline is reached.

questions.q: [image: pedestrian crossing warning sign] What does this warning sign mean?
opts: Playground area — no vehicles permitted beyond this point
School zone — reduce speed to 15 mph
Pedestrian crossing ahead — watch for people on foot
Bicycle lane crossing — yield to cyclists
questions.exp: A pedestrian crossing warning sign (yellow diamond, walking person) alerts drivers to a marked crosswalk or area where pedestrians frequently cross. Slow down and be prepared to yield.

questions.q: [image: slippery when wet sign] What does this warning sign indicate?
opts: Loose gravel on the road — slow down
The road surface is prone to becoming slippery when wet — reduce speed and avoid sudden maneuvers in wet weather
A car wash is ahead
Road paint markings may be wet — drive carefully
questions.exp: The slippery-when-wet sign (yellow diamond, skidding car) warns of road surfaces that become especially slick in rain. Reduce speed and avoid hard braking or sharp turning.

questions.q: [image: road work ahead sign] Orange diamond-shaped signs like this one are used to indicate:
opts: Detour routes only
General warning conditions on rural roads
Work zones — construction, maintenance, or utility work ahead
Speed advisories on highway ramps
questions.exp: Orange is the standard color for work-zone (construction/maintenance) signs. Traffic fines are often doubled in work zones. Slow down and follow all posted instructions.

questions.q: [image: red traffic light] What must you do at a traffic light showing this signal?
opts: Slow down and prepare to stop
Proceed through the intersection immediately
Come to a complete stop; remain stopped until the light turns green (or you may turn right on red if permitted)
Flash your headlights and proceed if the intersection is clear
questions.exp: A steady red light requires a full stop. You must remain stopped until the signal turns green. A right turn on red is allowed in NJ after stopping, unless a sign prohibits it.

questions.q: [image: yellow traffic light] What does a steady yellow traffic light mean?
opts: Speed up to clear the intersection before it turns red
The light is about to turn green — prepare to go
The signal is malfunctioning — treat as a four-way stop
The light is about to turn red — slow down and prepare to stop if you can do so safely
questions.exp: A yellow light warns that the signal is changing to red. You should slow down and stop if it is safe to do so. Do not accelerate to beat the light.

questions.q: [image: green traffic light] What does a steady green traffic light mean?
opts: You may proceed through the intersection — but first yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in it
You have absolute priority — proceed immediately
Cross traffic must stop — no need to check
It is safe to proceed at twice the posted speed limit
questions.exp: Green means you may go, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles already in the intersection. Green does not guarantee it is safe.

questions.q: [image: flashing red light] This traffic signal is flashing red. How should you treat it?
opts: Proceed without stopping — flashing signals are advisory only
Slow down significantly and proceed with caution
Stop completely; yield to all traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe (treat it as a stop sign)
Yield only to vehicles coming from the left
questions.exp: A flashing red light must be treated as a stop sign: come to a full stop, yield, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.q: [image: flashing yellow light] This traffic signal is flashing yellow. What should you do?
opts: Come to a complete stop and wait for a steady green
Slow down, be alert, and proceed with caution
Proceed at normal speed — you have priority
Come to a full stop and treat as a four-way stop
questions.exp: A flashing yellow light means slow down, use caution, and be prepared to yield. It warns of a potentially hazardous condition but does not require a full stop.

questions.q: What does a green arrow signal allow you to do?
opts: Proceed through the intersection in any direction
Turn only in the direction the arrow points — you have a protected turn and oncoming traffic is stopped
Proceed straight only; turning is prohibited
Yield to oncoming traffic and turn when safe
questions.exp: A green arrow provides a protected movement — conflicting traffic is stopped by a red signal. You may turn in the arrow's direction without yielding to oncoming vehicles.

questions.q: When can you legally make a right turn at a steady red light in New Jersey?
opts: Anytime the intersection is clear
Only between 6 PM and 6 AM
After coming to a full stop, yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic, and only if a sign does not prohibit it
Only when a green arrow is also displayed
questions.exp: NJ allows right turns on red after a complete stop, provided you yield to all pedestrians and vehicles with the right of way and no posted sign prohibits it.

questions.q: If a traffic signal is completely dark (power outage), how should you treat the intersection?
opts: The vehicle on the wider road always has priority
Proceed slowly without stopping
Treat it as a four-way stop — all vehicles must stop and yield in turn
The first vehicle to arrive automatically has right of way and may proceed without stopping
questions.exp: An inoperative traffic signal is treated as an all-way stop. Each vehicle must stop, then proceed in turn based on arrival order and right-of-way rules.

questions.q: A pedestrian signal showing a walking person (WALK) means:
opts: Pedestrians may begin crossing; vehicles must stop
Pedestrians should wait — don't start crossing
Only cyclists may cross here
Pedestrians must yield to turning vehicles
questions.exp: A WALK (walking person) signal indicates pedestrians may cross. Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are lawfully in the crosswalk.

questions.q: A flashing orange hand (DON'T WALK) pedestrian signal means:
opts: Pedestrians must stop immediately and wait
Pedestrians who have not started crossing should wait; those already crossing should finish quickly
All pedestrians must return to the curb
Vehicles may now proceed through the intersection
questions.exp: A flashing DON'T WALK signal means don't start crossing. Pedestrians already in the crosswalk should complete their crossing as quickly as possible.

questions.q: Double solid yellow center lines on a road mean:
opts: Passing is permitted when the way is clear
The road is divided — drive to the right of both lines
Neither direction of traffic may pass
Only vehicles going in the direction of travel may pass
questions.exp: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing in either direction. They mark roads where passing is considered too dangerous — such as on curves, hills, or narrow two-lane roads.

questions.q: A broken (dashed) yellow centerline means:
opts: You may pass if the way is clear and it is safe to do so
Passing is prohibited in both directions
The road ends ahead
It is a HOV (high-occupancy vehicle) lane
questions.exp: A broken yellow centerline indicates that passing is permitted when it is safe. Check for oncoming traffic and sufficient sight distance before passing.

questions.q: A solid yellow line on YOUR side of the center means:
opts: You may pass with caution
You may NOT pass — passing is prohibited from your side of the road
The road is one-way
Oncoming traffic must yield to you
questions.exp: A solid yellow line on your side prohibits you from passing. The line on the other side determines whether drivers coming from the opposite direction may pass.

questions.q: White lane markings on a roadway are used to:
opts: Separate traffic moving in opposite directions
Mark the edge of the road on the right side only
Separate lanes of traffic traveling in the same direction
Indicate no-passing zones
questions.exp: White markings divide traffic traveling in the same direction. Yellow markings divide traffic traveling in opposite directions.

questions.q: A solid white line between lanes means:
opts: You must not change lanes at all on this road
You should avoid changing lanes here — lane changes are discouraged though not absolutely prohibited
You must increase your speed to match surrounding traffic before changing lanes
Passing is permitted on this side only
questions.exp: A solid white line discourages lane changes at that location (e.g., near an intersection or where merging would be dangerous). A broken white line indicates lane changes are permitted.

questions.q: What does a white stop bar painted across a traffic lane indicate?
opts: The end of a bicycle lane
Where you must stop your vehicle at a stop sign or red light
A crosswalk for pedestrians only
A no-parking zone at an intersection
questions.exp: A white stop bar marks the exact point where a vehicle must stop at a sign or signal. If there is no stop bar, stop at the crosswalk line or the edge of the intersecting roadway.

questions.q: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), who has the right of way?
opts: The vehicle traveling at the highest speed
The larger vehicle
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
questions.exp: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must yield to any vehicle already in or arriving from your right. If you arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right, that driver has the right of way.

questions.q: When making a left turn at a green light, you must yield to:
opts: Only pedestrians in the crosswalk
Only vehicles behind you
Oncoming vehicles proceeding straight through or turning right, and pedestrians
No one — you have the green light
questions.exp: A driver turning left must always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, even on a green light. A green light grants permission to proceed — it does not override right-of-way rules.

questions.q: When an emergency vehicle with its lights and siren activated approaches, you must:
opts: Speed up to clear the intersection quickly
Maintain your speed and allow it to pass when possible
Immediately pull to the right curb (or as far right as possible), stop, and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle passes
Stop only if you are in the vehicle's lane of travel
questions.exp: NJ law requires drivers to immediately pull to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle (police, fire, EMS) with lights and siren approaches. Remain stopped until it passes.

questions.q: NJ's Move Over Law requires drivers to do what when approaching a stationary emergency or service vehicle with lights flashing on the side of the road?
opts: Stop completely and wait until the vehicle moves
Speed up to pass the scene quickly
Move over one lane away from the vehicle if safe; if not, slow down significantly below the posted speed limit
Activate your hazard lights and maintain your current speed
questions.exp: NJ's Move Over Law requires drivers approaching a stationary authorized emergency vehicle, law enforcement vehicle, tow truck, or highway maintenance vehicle with lights flashing to move over one lane (if safe) or slow to a safe speed.

questions.q: Pedestrians crossing in a marked or unmarked crosswalk:
opts: Must yield to all turning vehicles
Have the right of way only when the pedestrian signal shows WALK
Have the right of way and drivers must yield to them
May only cross when no vehicles are within 200 feet
questions.exp: NJ law gives pedestrians the right of way in all crosswalks — marked or unmarked. Drivers must yield when pedestrians are lawfully crossing.

questions.q: When must you stop for a stopped school bus with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended?
opts: Only if you are directly behind the bus
Only on undivided roads in both directions; on divided highways only vehicles behind the bus must stop
On all roads in both directions, with no exception
Only during school hours (7 AM – 4 PM)
questions.exp: On undivided roads, all traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus with lights flashing. On a divided highway (with a physical barrier), only traffic behind the bus must stop; oncoming traffic on the other side of the barrier may proceed.

questions.q: Yellow pavement markings are used to:
opts: Mark the right edge of the roadway
Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction
Indicate no-passing zones only
Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions
questions.exp: Yellow pavement markings always separate traffic traveling in opposite directions. White markings separate traffic traveling in the same direction.

questions.q: A regulatory sign is typically:
opts: Yellow or orange with a diamond shape
Green with white text showing route information
White (or red) with black or red text/symbols conveying a legal requirement
Blue with white symbols indicating services
questions.exp: Regulatory signs (such as speed limits, stop, yield, and no-turn signs) are typically white with black or red markings and have the force of law. Disobeying them can result in a traffic violation.

questions.q: When entering a roundabout (traffic circle), you must yield to:
opts: Vehicles entering from the right
All vehicles already traveling inside the roundabout
The largest vehicle, regardless of position
Vehicles entering from the left
questions.exp: In a roundabout, traffic already circulating inside has the right of way. You must yield upon entry until there is a safe gap. Travel counterclockwise inside the circle.

questions.q: What color and shape are most warning signs?
opts: Red octagons
White rectangles with red borders
Yellow diamonds (or pennants and pentagons for special cases)
Green rectangles
questions.exp: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols and are usually diamond-shaped. Exceptions include the school zone pentagon and the no-passing pennant, which are also yellow.

questions.q: Blue signs on highways are used to indicate:
opts: Speed advisories and construction zones
State and US route numbers
Services available at the next exit — such as gas, food, lodging, and hospitals
Tourist attractions and historical sites
questions.exp: Blue highway signs identify available services such as fuel, food, lodging, and medical facilities at upcoming exits. Brown signs are used for recreational and cultural attractions.
